anomalies.observed: The PMEG3030EP Schottky D1 is drawn with its cathode (bar side) tied to the +5V rail and its anode tied to the servo power rail (the node feeding J8 pin 2, J4 pin 2 and the C6/C2/C4/C3 100 µF bank). This is the opposite orientation to the correctly-drawn series input diode D2 (SS54), whose cathode sits on the +5V side so that current flows from the external jack into +5V.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, this diode must conduct FROM +5V INTO the servo rail: 'From +5V, a second diode D2 (PMEG3030EP ...) feeds a dedicated servo power rail backed by four 100 µF capacitors (C1–C4) before reaching J3/J8 pin 2.' The anode should be on the +5V side and the cathode on the servo-rail side.

evidence.quote: From +5V, a second diode D2 (PMEG3030EP, annotated "3A 360mV" in the schematic — a low-forward-voltage-drop Schottky) feeds a dedicated servo power rail backed by four 100 µF capacitors (C1–C4) before reaching J3/J8 pin 2.
D1 PMEG3030EP 3A 360mV — cathode bar at the +5V node, anode at the J8.2/J4.2/C6/C2/C4/C3 servo-rail node (sheet m5-pantilt.kicad_sch, page 1, region B/C column 4).

anomalies.impact: With the diode reversed, +5V cannot forward-bias into the servo rail, so the bulk-capacitor bank and the servo headers' power pin (pin 2) are never energized from the board's 5V supply. Servos would receive no power (and the rail could instead back-feed +5V through D1), defeating the inrush-buffering function the spec describes.
